This chain of targets culminates in the muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M1, indicating a possible indirect interaction. The mechanism appears to involve a two-step process, where 5-deoxyflavanone acts as a modulator of a receptor that is itself a target of another compound. This suggests that 5-deoxyflavanone may influence the activity of muscarinic receptors through a downstream pathway involving Sphingosine 1-phosphate. The evidence supports a complex, multi-target interaction, with the receptor M1 being a final endpoint in this cascade.
